purpose: Authored runtime-ready environmental profiles, separated from botanical evidence. Load explicitly through --profiles data/vegetation-environment.v1.json. This JSON-only pass does not change the catalogue adapter or preset loader.
temperatureSemantics: Reference city/set temperature must represent a long-term annual mean, then elevation cooling is applied. Not instantaneous weather, daily extremes, growing-season temperature, cold-hardiness zone, or tissue temperature.

scoring.temperature: Existing triangular response: 0 at/outside minimum/maximum, 1 at optimum; linear interpolation.
scoring.slope: Existing slope response: 1 at 0..optimum, then linear decline toward maximum.
scoring.combined: min(temperatureScore, slopeScore); hard Allowed is independent of soft Score.
scoring.hardSlope: Allowed is false only when exact local slope > terrain.maximumSlopeDegrees; equality is permitted. At the cap the soft slope score is still positive.

suggestedSetDefault.note: Authoring recommendation, not automatically wired by this file. Effective cap is min(set cap, profile cap); use a 60-degree set override to allow shrubs on steeper terrain. A 45-degree set caps shrubs too.

modellingNotes: All exact triangle endpoints and peaks are authoring choices, even where anchored by observed climate distributions; occurrence statistics are not growth optima or mortality thresholds.
Slope caps are conservative placement policies, not researched universal survival bounds. All trees currently use 45 degrees and shrubs 60 degrees; stored per asset for future adjustment.
No researched temperature range is promoted to a hard temperature exclusion; a zero soft temperature score alone does not make Allowed false.
Broad elevation bounds are solver safety defaults, not species altitude limits; avoid counting altitude twice through climate and an invented biological altitude cap.
Raw source dataset remains separate to avoid presenting model assumptions as measured botanical facts.
London plane uses Platanus, superseding the historical Acer campestre interpretation. The unmatched EuropeanSpruce mesh is provisional and remains excluded from starter presets.

slope-pine-study.title: Influence of slope on root system anchorage of Pinus yunnanensis
slope-pine-study.finding: Study includes established pines at 42–43 degrees; it does not establish a universal maximum slope.

slope-shrub-study.title: The Response of Spartium junceum Roots to Slope: Anchorage and Gene Factors
slope-shrub-study.finding: Experiments with a shrub used 45-degree tilted pots; this does not establish a 60-degree survival limit or validate all shrubs.
